page: OVHcloud c2-15-flex is a compute-oriented virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture running at a base clock speed of 3.0 GHz, configured with 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading (4 vCPUs total). Memory allocation is 15.0 GB of RAM, yielding 3.75 GB per core. The server includes 50 GB of bundled local SSD storage and features no GPU acceleration. CPU feature flags provide AVX, AES-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, while lacking newer AVX-512 extensions and hardware SHA instructions.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier throughput across standard computational tasks. The instance records average-tier outcomes in single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, Clang compilation, and PassMark database operations, along with a Redis SET speed of 6.63 million operations per second. However, compute performance degrades in highly vectorized or modern floating-point workloads, showing bottom-tier scores in PassMark CPU encryption, Geekbench ray tracing, and Geekbench image processing. Memory throughput delivers 40.72 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 33.79 GB/sec for uncached writes. Inference benchmarks on 7B parameter language models show poor responsiveness due to limited CPU architectural vector capabilities and the absence of discrete accelerator hardware.

With its 1:3.75 vCPU-to-memory ratio, dedicated core allocation, and bundled local SSD, OVHcloud c2-15-flex delivers predictable processing without hyperthread contention. It provides balanced hardware density for stable development pipelines, background task processing, utility databases, and moderate web applications, though workloads reliant on newer instruction set extensions or GPU acceleration will face performance limitations.

The hardware profile is configured with 15.0 GB of system memory (3.75 GB per core) and includes a 50 GB local SSD without discrete GPU hardware. The server provides AVX and AES vector extensions while lacking modern AVX-512 capabilities. Benchmarks reflect steady middle-tier execution across integer tasks, compilation with Clang, and Redis caching workloads, but show weak throughput on ray tracing, encryption, and larger language model inference.
